walkthroughs.body_html:
Foundations in Biology — a core area of A-Level Biology.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Foundations in Biology brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Foundations in Biology.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Which scientist proposed 'omnis cellula e cellula' (all cells from pre-existing cells)?
options: Schleiden
Schwann
Virchow
Hooke

mcqs.q: The fluid mosaic model of the cell membrane was proposed in 1972 by:
options: Watson and Crick
Singer and Nicolson
Schleiden and Schwann
Margulis and Lovelock

mcqs.q: Why is the cohesion-tension theory critical for water transport in plants?
options: Cohesion-tension describes how water diffuses freely between cells.
Hydrogen bonds between water molecules keep the water column unbroken under tension, so transpiration can pull water up from the roots.
Cohesion-tension explains how plants store water in the xylem like a reservoir.
DNA ligase reads the gene and translates it into protein.

mcqs.q: How do insulin and glucagon work together to regulate blood glucose?
options: They are antagonistic — insulin lowers blood glucose (cells take up glucose, store as glycogen); glucagon raises it (glycogen broken back down to glucose).
Insulin and glucagon both lower blood glucose using different mechanisms.
DNA ligase reads the gene and translates it into protein.
Insulin works on muscles and glucagon works on the brain.

mcqs.q: What is the role of DNA ligase when inserting a gene into a plasmid?
options: Cohesion-tension explains how plants store water in the xylem like a reservoir.
It forms phosphodiester bonds that join the gene to the cut plasmid, sealing the recombinant DNA.
DNA ligase cuts the plasmid open so the gene can be inserted.
DNA ligase reads the gene and translates it into protein.
